correctness.rationale: All allowed m,c and N=0 boundary checked in the proof. Generators below F+1 and in [F+1,2m-1] are forced; those in [2m+1,F+m] correspond exactly to absent sums from B+B. The fixed-genus coefficient count uses disjoint two-element pair choices. For r/N to p in (0,1), hypergeometric prefixes converge, and Bernoulli lower coupling bounds missing-sum tails exponentially, proving total variation and uniform integrability. Infinite Bernoulli odd/even missing probabilities sum to (1-p)(2-p)/p^2. Independent exhaustive finite checks corroborate identities but are not substituted for proof.

value.rationale: Embedding dimension and genus are standard, structurally distinct numerical-semigroup invariants. The exact hypergeometric mean resolves the generator count within each finite (F,m,g) slice, while the conditional total-variation law shows nontrivial O(1) fluctuations about the deterministic genus baseline. The result bridges contemporary triple-counting and established random-sumset statistics in a uniform infinite parameter regime, not a single computed example.
